SAD Study Notes

 

Phase: 1

 

Purpose and Study Drug

 

This study is testing a potential new treatment for Ulcerative Colitis which is an inflammatory bowel disease that causes chronic or recurring inflammation of the innermost lining of the colon and rectum. 

 

We are testing this study in healthy volunteers first. By studying the investigational product in healthy individuals initially, it allows researchers to understand its safety, how it behaves in the body, and how the immune system responds to it before it is tested in people with Ulcerative Colitis.

elements.name: question13b
elements.html:
Study Design

 

Participants will be randomly allocated to receive an oral tablet containing either the study drug or a placebo (Cohort 3 PT's will get 2 doses, all other SAD cohorts is 1 dose). The placebo is a tablet that does not contain any active medication. It is used for comparison so researchers can properly evaluate the effects of the study drug. This study is double-blinded, meaning neither you nor the study staff will know whether you receive the study drug or placebo.

 

If you are eligible following this phone pre-screen, you will attend the clinic for screening assessments. These include blood tests, vital signs, ECGs and a physical examination to confirm eligibility.

 

SAD Cohorts 

 

If eligible:

  • You will be admitted to the clinic for a 4-night inpatient stay (Day -1 to Day 4).
  • You will receive a single dose of the study drug or placebo on Day 1.
  • After discharge on Day 4, you will have 1 follow-up visit on Day 8.

 

SAD Cohort 3 - Food Effect Cohort 

 

If eligible:

  • You will be admitted to the clinic for a 8-night inpatient stay (Day -1 to Day 8).
  • In total you will receive 2 doses of either the study drug or placebo through the study. Your first dose will be on Day 1 of your in-clinic stay under fasted conditions. The second dose will be done on Day 5 which before you are given your allocated drug, participants will consume a high-calorie, high-fat meal in order for study staff to evaluate the meal's effect on absorption of the study drug. This meal will contain animal derived products so participants in this cohort must not be vegetarian, vegan or have any other dietary restrictions.
  • After discharge on Day 8, you will have 1 follow-up visit on Day 12.

 

We are currently recruiting for:

 

Cohort 3 Sentinel Food Effect: [FILLED]

Your in-clinic stay will be from the 3rd - 11th of December.

 

You would then return to the clinic for a follow-up visit on the 15th of December (± 1 day).

 

Cohort 3 ROC Food Effect: [FILLED]

Your in-clinic stay will be from the 9th - 17th of December.

 

You would then return to the clinic for a follow-up visit on the 21st of December (± 1 day).

 

 

Could you please confirm your availability for the dates?

 

 

Additional Information:

Screening time - 2-3 hrs

Follow-up visit time - 1.5 hrs

In summary, if you are dosed in the study and complete all visits, you will receive a total amount of approximately $3,000.

 

If you are an eligible alternate, and do not get dosed, you will receive a partial reimbursement of $900. This includes the screening payment of $300.

You would receive:

In summary, if you are dosed in the study and complete all visits, you will receive a total amount of approximately $4,760.

 

If you are an eligible alternate, and do not get dosed, you will receive a partial reimbursement of $820. This includes the screening payment of $300.

 

Payment Timeline -

 

Reimbursement will be paid as a lump sum at the end of study, approximately within 3-5 business day after the final follow-up visit.

elements.name: question47

Study Design

 

Participants will be randomly allocated to receive 10 oral doses of either the study drug or a placebo. Neither you nor the clinical team will know which one you receive.

 

If you are eligible following this phone pre-screen, you will attend the clinic for screening assessments. These include blood tests, vital signs, ECGs and a physical examination to confirm eligibility.

 

MAD Cohorts 

 

If eligible:

  • You will be admitted to the clinic for a 13-night inpatient stay (Day -1 to Day 13).
  • You will receive a daily dose of the study drug or placebo on Days 1 - 10.
  • After discharge on Day 13, you will have 1 follow-up visit on Day 17 (±1 day).

 

Flexible Sigmoidoscopies

 

On days 3 and 10 of your in-clinic stay, you will have a short flexible sigmoidoscopy to examine the lower bowel. Preparation involves an overnight fast and an enema before the procedure. You will receive sedation for comfort while a thin flexible camera is used to collect several tiny, superficial samples from the bowel lining for study testing. The procedure usually takes around 10 to 20 minutes and you will recover in the unit afterwards.

 

Are you comfortable undergoing these two procedures as part of the study?

 

We are currently recruiting for:

 

MAD 6 Group 2

 

Your in-clinic stay will be from the 6th - 19th of December.

 

You would then return to the clinic for a follow-up visit on the 23rd of December (±1 day.

elements.name: question58
elements.html:
To take part, you need to be generally healthy. If you rely on daily prescription medication, you’re unlikely to be eligible for this study.

 

You can’t take any prescription medication or OTC medications (including herbal supplements) within 14 days (or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer) before dosing. 

 

This study is particularly strict with medications and supplements. We are looking for PTs that can act as a completely clean slate so they shouldn't be taking anything (besides contraception and occasional paracetamol) 14 days before dosing. 

 

Indigo naturalis is a particular concern as it acts on the same receptors as the study drug.

 

Contraception and occasional Panadol is ok!

elements.name: question20b
elements.title: Before we wrap up, I’d like to share details about our referral program. If you refer someone to us you can receive up to $250 if they enrol and participate in the study. Would you like to hear more?

elements.name: question21b
elements.html:
Great! Here's how it works:

 

To refer someone, you will need to provide them with a unique referral ID. The person you refer will need to provide us this ID either when they sign up on our website, or when they speak to us over the phone. This ID is essential, as it ensures we can track and reimburse you for any referrals.

 

For each person you refer who comes in for an in-person screening visit, you'll receive $50. If they go on to enrol and participate in the study, you'll earn an additional $200.

 

There's no limit- you can refer as many people as you'd like, as long as you have an exisiting relationship with them. It's important to note that you cannot advertise for referrals. This program is based on personal connections, so please only refer people you know.

 

If you're interested, we can set up your Unique Referral ID today if you would like (the unique referral ID is REF[p number]. E.g., REFP14471)

 

Who do you know you might be interested in this trial? (if they don't know anyone for this trial, they can also refer someone to any other trial)

 

Would you like us to send you an email that you can forward on to them?
